questions.q: What two methods must a custom torch.utils.data.Dataset subclass implement?
options: __init__ and __call__
__len__ and __getitem__
forward and backward
load and save
questions.explain: __len__ returns the total number of examples, and __getitem__ returns a single example given an index. Together these are all a Dataset needs to define.

questions.q: When you iterate over a DataLoader, what does each yielded item represent?
options: A single example from the dataset
The entire dataset at once
A batch of examples stacked along a new leading dimension, with batch_size controlling how many
A randomly selected subset the size of the whole dataset
questions.explain: DataLoader groups individual examples from the Dataset into batches; iterating yields one batch at a time, each with shape (batch_size, ...).

questions.q: Why should shuffle=True typically be used for a training DataLoader but shuffle=False for a validation/test DataLoader?
options: Shuffling is required by PyTorch and cannot be disabled

Training benefits from randomized example order each epoch to avoid biasing learning toward a fixed order, while validation/test evaluation doesn't need randomness and benefits from reproducible, consistent ordering
shuffle=False makes validation run on the GPU instead of CPU
shuffle=True changes the batch_size automatically
questions.explain: Shuffling training data each epoch prevents the model from learning spurious patterns tied to data order. Validation and test sets don't need shuffling since you're just measuring performance, not learning from the order.

questions.q: What does the num_workers argument to DataLoader control?
options: The number of GPUs used for training
The number of background worker processes that prepare upcoming batches in parallel, which can speed up training when data loading (e.g. disk I/O, decoding) is slow
The number of epochs to train for
The number of layers in the model
questions.explain: num_workers spawns subprocesses that load and prepare batches concurrently with the main training loop, overlapping data preparation with GPU computation.

questions.q: When is TensorDataset the right choice instead of writing a custom Dataset subclass?
options: Only when training on a GPU
When your data already exists as one or more tensors with matching first-dimension sizes, and you just need to index them together
Only when batch_size is 1
Never — custom Dataset subclasses are always required
questions.explain: TensorDataset is a built-in convenience Dataset that wraps tensors already in memory, indexing them together without requiring a custom __len__/__getitem__ implementation.
